title: Everything Tiny
rule: Make everything tiny, small enough to fit in a teacup.

title: Seen From Above
rule: Draw everything as if you were looking straight down on it from above.

title: Up Close
rule: Draw the subject so close that it runs off the edges of the page.
phrases: let the edges cut it off

title: One Light Only
rule: Pick one spot for the light and make every shadow point away from it.
phrases: every shadow on the far side

title: Two Pencils: Moonlight
rule: Use only a dark blue and White, as if the moon were the only light.

title: Warm Colours Only
rule: Use only warm colours, and press hard on the last layer so it shines.

title: Two Pencils: Brown and White
rule: Use only Dark Brown and White, on tan or brown paper if you have some.

title: Three Pencils Only
rule: Use only the three pencils dealt, and layer them to mix any other colours.

title: Two Pencils: Opposite Colours
rule: Use only these two opposite colours: colour with the first, then layer the second over it for the shadows.

title: Postage Stamp Size
rule: Draw the picture the size of a postage stamp, with a zigzag edge all round.
phrases: about the size of your thumb
a zigzag edge like a stamp

title: Seen Through a Window
rule: Draw the scene as if through a window, with one pale streak of reflection across the glass.
phrases: one white streak on the glass

title: Half Hidden
rule: Hide half of the subject behind something in front of it.

title: Through a Keyhole
rule: Draw the scene in a keyhole shape, as if peeping through a door, and let its edges fade to bare paper.

title: Hide a Small Animal
rule: Hide a small animal somewhere in the picture for someone else to find.
phrases: a mouse, a bird or a snail

title: One Long Line
rule: Draw the outline in one long line without lifting the pencil, then colour as usual.

title: Your Other Hand First
rule: Draw with the hand you don't write with for the first five minutes, then swap back.

title: Draw It Again
rule: Draw this subject again in its new place and light, then compare it with your first drawing.
phrases: a new place and a new light

title: Three Views
rule: Draw the subject three times across the page: from the front, the side and the back.
phrases: three small drawings in a row

title: Tall and Narrow
rule: Fit the picture into a tall, narrow strip the shape of a bookmark.

title: One Colour Family
rule: Use only three shades of one colour: a light, a middle and a dark.
